LightRAG round two: cross-patent node audit

# LightRAG round two: source and semantic audit of cross-patent nodes

2026-10-30 · existing v1.5.7 snapshot · read-only audit · new API cost $0

Of 612 nodes, **38 nodes (6.21%)** come from two or more patents. After item-by-item review, **32 support reasonable class/concept sharing**; another **6 juxtapose homonyms or document-local roles in one ID**. The latter are not “6 confirmed wrong merges”: 5 of them are sensitive to how ontology granularity and role scope are interpreted.

**Scope completed:** 38/38 nodes, 98/98 node–patent sources, 307 per-node adjacent-edge reviews (266 distinct actual edges). All 98 representative quotes were checked against the specific original text, claim/abstract and the actual source chunk. The original graph, the original index and the old reports were not changed; no index was rebuilt, no new query run, and no LLM/embedding called.

## Statistics and decision boundaries

| Final category | Nodes | Share of the 38 multi-source nodes |
| ---|---|--- |
| More specific shared technical concept | 3 | 7.9% |
| Reasonably shared broad class | 29 | 76.3% |
| Homonym / document-local role juxtaposition | 6 | 15.8% |
| Insufficient evidence | 0 | 0.0% |

“Shared broad class” covers generic classes such as Processor, Memory, Server, System. Concrete instances in different patents are not interchangeable, but they can share a superclass; a generic name is not an error in itself. The more specific shared concepts are Tokens, Labels and Label in the query context. The two kinds total 32, and none is judged wrong because its name is generic.

**Ontology sensitivity:** the 6 juxtaposed nodes are First User, Second User, Third User, Event, Token and Network. Token's difference between “anonymisation substitute / query token” is the clearest; the other 5 keep a legitimate broad-class reading. Under that reading the counts become shared technical concepts 3, shared broad classes 34, homonym juxtaposition 1. Neither count can be used as a code defect rate or an entity-resolution accuracy.

This is an AI-assisted item-by-item content review, with a second AI review of 7 key nodes; it is **not an independent human gold standard**. High/medium confidence is a qualitative judgment. The first assessment listed 2 kinds of storage media as more specific concepts; to keep the same granularity as other storage media and Processor/Memory, they were finally unified as shared broad classes. Both the first assessment and the decision are kept; this does not change the total of reasonable sharing or the number of juxtaposed nodes.

## How the source statistics are reproduced

The 20 patents on information retrieval, recommendation, contextual ranking and similar topics, selected purposively from the first 100 rows of the `lj408/Dis2Pat` dataset, are reused; not a random representative sample. Nothing was downloaded again this time. The actual snapshot has 20 patents, 48 chunks, 612 nodes, 994 edges. Starting from the union of a node's `source_id` and the complete `entity_chunks.chunk_ids`, publication numbers are grouped by `text_chunks.full_doc_id → the publication header of full_docs`; several chunks and path aliases of the same patent count once. The node's `file_path` is then cross-checked, without pairing by position in the separated lists.

`&lt;SEP&gt;` is the separator of the saved fields. Of the 38 nodes, 28 come from 2 patents, 6 from 3, 3 from 5, 1 from 9. A node has at most 14 chunks; missing mappings, document conflicts, differences between the source KV and graph fields, and path correspondence differences are all 0. All 48 actual chunks can be located verbatim in the complete indexed text they belong to. No source-list truncation occurs in this snapshot; this does not mean that truncation cannot occur at any scale.

47 extraction responses are read from the original cache; US9218390B2-chunk-000 was once truncated at the output cap and not cached, so the saved request and raw response of call 191 complete the review, with the `finish_reason=length` caveat kept. No model was called to fill gaps. For all 98 node–patent sources the raw entity extraction line with that name was found. The audit covers the title, the complete abstract and the claims of the index at the time, not the unindexed complete specification.

## Three representative cases

### 1. Genuine sharing: Tokens (N032, 2 patents)

Both patents split a query into tokens and assign labels: one serves cross-language query patterns, the other parsing of geographic search queries. They share the technical concept of query tokens; this does not mean that the two queries or algorithm instances are the same.

**US8655901B1 · Claim 15**
segmenting a given query among the collection into one or more tokens in the first language, wherein each token includes one or more terms from the given query;
Word/phrase segments of a first-language query, bound to query-pattern component labels; the translation order is used to recover the target-language pattern.
Source chunk: US8655901B1-chunk-001

**US9218390B2 · Claim 1**
receiving an input query, wherein the input query comprises a series of tokens; assigning a label to each of a plurality of the tokens;
The token sequence of an input geographic web search query; the labels are used for conditional-random-field parsing.
Source chunk: US9218390B2-chunk-000

Actual edge 704 is `Tokens — Labels` and keeps both sources; the corresponding singular edge 251 `Token — Label` is also supported by both query patents. In the current graph singular and plural are different IDs; this task does not evaluate synonym nodes that should have been merged but were not.

### 2. Reasonable but broad: Processor (N019, 9 patents)

All 9 texts give the processor the hardware role of executing instructions, so sharing the Processor class is reasonable; the processor instances in each patent and their duties cannot be aligned on that basis. Its 25 actual adjacent edges were reviewed against their own sources; cross-document adjacency was not automatically counted as an error.

**US10778629B2 · Claim 10**
transferring, from the server, the data to a processor for generating relationship data by determining a relationship strength associated with each pair of users
Receives data from the server and generates relationship-strength/relationship data for user pairs.
Source chunk: US10778629B2-chunk-000, US10778629B2-chunk-001

**US11423041B2 · Claim 1**
a memory, storing program instructions that when executed by the at least one processor
Executes instructions stored in memory to implement the data catalogue.
Source chunk: US11423041B2-chunk-000

Original texts, claims, source_ids and adjacent edges of the other 7 patents: see the expanded item N019 and the per-source CSV.

### 3. A clear homonym juxtaposition: Token (N017, 3 patents)

**US8655901B1 · Claim 1**
segmenting a given query among the collection into one or more tokens in the first language, wherein each token includes one or more terms from the given query
A segment of words in a query, labelled by query-pattern component, used for cross-language pattern mining.
Source chunk: US8655901B1-chunk-000

**US9118735B1 · Claim 14**
anonymizing results based on replacing an identifier associated with the second user with a token
An anonymisation substitute value replacing a user identifier.
Source chunk: US9118735B1-chunk-001

**US9218390B2 · Claim 18**
receiving an input query, wherein the input query comprises a series of tokens; assigning a label to each of a plurality of the tokens
A labellable unit in a geographic search query, used in building the CRF model.
Source chunk: US9218390B2-chunk-002

The same `Token` node merges two meanings, the anonymisation substitute value and the NLP query token. Actual edge 193 is `Second User — Token` (only US9118735B1), edge 251 is `Token — Label` (only US8655901B1, US9218390B2). The shared node therefore allows paths across meanings to form; both edges are still supported in their own sources.

**No direct edge “an anonymous user must have query labels” was added or observed, and no query was run this time to show propagation into a wrong answer.** This is a checkable risk of word-sense distinction / source scope and cannot be classed directly as a LightRAG code bug.

## Adjacent-edge check: semantic conflation kept apart from error propagation

Among the 266 relevant actual edges, no unsupported edge or answer propagation caused by cross-patent merging was confirmed. Only 4 edges actually have cross-patent sources: Weight—Characteristic, Token—Label, Processor—Memory, Tokens—Labels; their source clauses must be interpreted one by one, and no merged description can be attributed to every patent.

**There are also 3 within-source role warnings:** US9514120B1 claim 18 explicitly has the `server computing machine` perform combine, sort and update; chunk002 starts in the middle of a sentence, and the saved raw extraction and graph edges 495, 502 and 517 use `Apparatus` as the acting subject. This is an observed inconsistency of role granularity, first appearing in single-patent raw extraction. A reading as a summary of the overall apparatus's function still needs qualification; it cannot be attributed to cross-patent merging, and no boundary control or new QA in this run demonstrates causal propagation. The Apparatus node itself is still a shared broad class.

## Full evidence, expanded

N001 · Data Processing System · shared broad class · 2 patents

**Decision:** both use the term for a software/computer system performing data processing: one processes geographic visualisation of IP rights, the other selects advertisements by user interest and keyword weights. The purposes and local systems differ, but the common superclass of computer data-processing system explains the same-name node; no original text or graph edge shows that the two are the same deployed instance.

**Class and instance:** a common system class, not the same system instance. The merged description lists each task side by side with &lt;SEP&gt;; not all components can be asserted of a single system in either patent at once; the shared node only creates potential cross-document adjacency.

**Type in the original graph:** artifact; **confidence:** high; **files:** US9298709B2.txt, US9304738B1.txt

**US9298709B2 · Claim 1**
A data processing system to visualise data from an IP rights database comprising:
A computer system that uses an IP-rights database as its data source and filters and updates visualisations within the visible map area.
Source chunk: US9298709B2-chunk-000

**US9304738B1 · Claim 13**
a data processing system having one or more processors and memory, the data processing system configured to:
A processing system that receives advertising interest signals, identifies and weights keywords, ranks and selects advertisements.
Source chunk: US9304738B1-chunk-000, US9304738B1-chunk-001

**Adjacent-edge review:** all 19 adjacent edges were re-checked, grouped by their own source_id: 0–8 are IP visualisation; 9–18 are keyword advertisement selection. No actual edge attributing map components directly to the advertising patent was found. The shared node allows combined paths, but no saved query shows that propagation happened.

N002 · Mobile Device · shared broad class · 2 patents

**Decision:** both sources use the class of mobile terminal: one produces short messages/queries and receives context data, the other has a camera and screen for social face search. Hardware configuration and task differ, but both belong to the common superclass of mobile device; there is no mutually exclusive word sense or assertion of the same device identity.

**Class and instance:** a shared mobile-device class; it does not mean that the device instances of the two patents are the same, nor that every mobile device has a camera. Adjacencies such as Smart Phone and Tablet should keep their source qualification.

**Type in the original graph:** artifact; **confidence:** high; **files:** US8509827B2.txt, US8917913B2.txt

N003 · Server · shared broad class · 5 patents

**Decision:** all five sources support a computing/server-side role, respectively handling email relationship data, collecting context data, finding people through social networks, streaming video, and classifying typographical errors. Different services do not make the word server conflict; it can be classed as a broad server class. The specific executor of the Server→User Interface edge is weak; it is recorded separately and not escalated to a cross-patent conflation.

**Class and instance:** a shared server superclass; it does not mean that one server runs five systems at once, nor can the identities of the five services be merged on that basis. The server associated with the provider and the server receiving short messages may also be different deployment roles within the same document; the original texts do not require them to be the same.

N004 · Database · shared broad class · 3 patents

**Decision:** all three sources mean a database that can store/query data: backup management data, received context data, and advertising keywords with weights, respectively. The different stored data does not change the common storage-class meaning of database; it cannot be judged a conflation only because the neighbours differ.

The definitions and associated behaviour of the two roles are constrained by in-document ordinals rather than being one stable technical role across documents. Classing them under a broad User class accommodates both but does not show that the two Second User placeholders have corresponding identities or are interchangeable; the single ID loses this local role scope. It is not claimed that the model actually took them for the same real person.

**Class and instance:** a local role placeholder, not a known individual, and not an explicitly modelled global “second user” ontology class. contextual_conflation is used only for this collision of role scopes; if a caller strictly uses it as a polymorphic broad User class by source, errors can be avoided, hence medium confidence.

**Type in the original graph:** person; **confidence:** medium; **files:** US9118735B1.txt, US9304738B1.txt

N012 · Third User · homonym / role juxtaposition · 2 patents

**Decision:** in one patent Third User is the recipient, distinct from the first two users, whose request triggers the selection of advertising content; in the other it is the bridge in the first user's social network who meets the location/consent-to-share conditions. “Third” is a document-local role name; the texts give no unified role definition across scenarios. Abstracting only to User loses the meaning of “third participant”, which depends on the specific flow; the current single Person ID collects these local roles, which should not be directly interchanged. This is evidence of a scope collapse, not an assertion of the same person or evidence of cross-patent error propagation.

**Class and instance:** same-named local roles, not the same real individual; sharing the User superclass is reasonable in itself, but identity of Third User instances or roles cannot be inferred from it. No separate schema constraint forbids the broad-class reading, so this classification is not escalated to a definite program merge bug.

N016 · Event · homonym / role juxtaposition · 2 patents

**Decision:** the texts clearly present two event meanings: in US11423041B2 a data-processing event registered to a history object, triggered by conditions and causing an ETL job to run; in US9118735B1 an activity/event that a user claims to be attending and that can be used for location. The description of the current single Event ID lists both roles side by side, and the adjacent edges attach geographic location/attendance by people and subscription/trigger relations to the same node. Both can belong to a highly abstract “occurrence”, but that superclass does not support interchanging the current concrete relation roles; this classification is a need for semantic distinction, not proof of erroneous reasoning that exists.

**Class and instance:** an occurrence/event superclass could be established explicitly, keeping the two contextual meanings or subclasses of data-processing event and activity attended by people. The graph gives no formal ontology, so C3 expresses the review judgment that concrete meanings/scopes are collapsed in the current single ID; it does not prove that the class merge is wrong; if the node is presumed to be a broad class, shared_broad_class is also a reasonable reading. It is not claimed that several events within one patent are the same instance, nor is cross-source adjacency taken as the fact that people attend an ETL event.

N022 · Network · homonym / role juxtaposition · 2 patents

**Decision:** US8095432B1 claim 3 defines the asking member's social network with friends inside and non-friends outside; US9589231B2 claim 20 explicitly defines the composition of the network as the diagnosis-assistance system and the set of user devices connecting requesters/experts. The original entity descriptions follow these two different member domains, yet the final single node carries both friendship adjacent edges and device/system composition edges. Both can be abstracted as interconnected collections, so the classification keeps medium confidence; but such a very broad superclass does not express the different semantic constraints of the concrete member network and the device/system network.

**Class and instance:** the current label mixes two contextual meanings, a network of social members and a network of systems/devices. Network could be defined explicitly as the superclass “interconnected collection”, keeping the scope of subclasses/instances; under such an ontology, shared_broad_class is also a reasonable reading. The current graph gives no formal ontology, so C3 is not a proven semantic error or bug; this audit does not automatically read a global label as the same physical network or the same organisation.

**Type in the original graph:** organization; **confidence:** medium; **files:** US8095432B1.txt, US9589231B2.txt

## Reproduction and limitations

The evidence package keeps the original graph snapshot, GraphML, source KV, the 20 indexed texts and claims, the 47 cached extractions and the raw record of call 191; it also provides per-node / per-source CSV, complete JSON, all first reviews, decisions, verification results and a SHA256 list of the files. The statistics scripts use only the Python standard library: run `python3 round2_multisource_audit/scripts/build_inventory.py`, then `python3 round2_multisource_audit/scripts/validate_reviews.py --require-complete`. The semantic classification is the retained conclusion of the AI review; rerunning the statistics does not generate new human judgments automatically.

This is an exhaustive multi-source node audit of a single 20-patent graph, not an evaluation of general performance; there is no independent human re-annotation, query intervention or instance/sameAs gold standard. The boundary between generic classes and specific concepts, and the ontology choices for Event/Network and local ordinal roles, may all affect the classification. Complete sources do not mean that the claim-by-claim structure is modelled, nor that every merged summary has clause-level provenance.
